The study confirms that the H-MR-TVA utilisation guarantees up to 3-fold lower tower deflection amplitude than the passive TVA and up to 10-fold lower than the TVA locked. However, the H-MR-TVA uses 53% more working space than the passive TVA. The maximum actuator power is a fraction of a watt for the regarded solutions.

articleTitle: The Design of Controller for Swing Up Cart Pole Problem with Strongly Constrained Input
abstract: This paper presents an approach to designing the controller for the swing up cart pole problem. The approach used to solve the problem is a method based on Deep Reinforcement Learning. We taught an artificial neural network to control the plant as a controller. Furthermore, the input saturation is strongly limited to check the maximum possibilities of the controller. We investigated the control accuracy and the actor policy if the control signal was reduced. Our control goal was to reach the unstable equilibrium and keep that state starting from the stable state of the cart pole. That task was performed by one controller tested in an environment prepared by us, where the parameters of the cart pole are based on the real device. The results come from tests of many neural networks trained for different seed values.

articleTitle: Transformative Learning: Nurturing Novices to Experts through 3D Simulation and Virtual Reality in Education
abstract: Within the appearance of Industry 4.0 era, the industrial concepts have been changed a lot. Digital twin concept which is based on 3D simulation and virtual reality start to be implemented in every sector, especially in the automotive sector, where several scenarios and cases can be executed. This will increase the chance of errors and decrease the cycle time of delivering the product to the customer. Therefore, by using these solutions “3D simulation and virtual reality softwares”, the engineers will be much closer to the real process manufacturing, and they can predict more easily the gap and the mistakes in the production line. This paper presents the impact of 3D simulation and virtual reality on the industrial sector and highlights the importance of including these solutions in the education part, from early age, where the student can be an expert in designing and programming several scenarios using professional softwares. Two softwares are presented Visual Components for designing 3D automated processes, and SimLab for designing and visualizing a virtual environment through VR headset. The study will be described through practical tutorials, dedicated for education purposes.

articleTitle: Modeling And Control Strategies For Bicopter Type UAVs
abstract: This paper deals with the modeling and simulation of a Bicopter type UAV. It provides a detailed derivation of the mathematical model for both planar and spatial Bicopters based on the Euler-Lagrange equation and Newton's second law of motion. We have designed a trajectory controller for the planar model and a cascade controller for the spatial model. Simulation results are presented and discussed. For realtime implementation knowing the position of the system is essential. In this regard, the article outlines a position determination principle based on inertial sensors, where the states will be estimated and filtered using a Kalman filter.

articleTitle: Theoretical Considerations on the Achievability of Uniform Distribution of Irradiance on the Surface
abstract: The growing demand for industrial illuminators with various parameters prompts work on new solutions. One of them is to build an illuminator that emits electromagnetic radiation to the surface in a uniform manner in terms of irradiation intensity. The article presents mathematical considerations regarding the possibility of achieving uniform irradiance on a surface perpendicular to the optical axis of an LED emitting Lambertian luminous intensity radiation. The article also presents a theoretical photometric solid that would allow achieving uniform irradiance on the surface perpendicular to the optical axis of the LED. Theoretically, it is possible to achieve uniformity on a surface with a different shape, as presented.

articleTitle: Georeferencing System for Maneuvering of Autonomous Truck in Mining Environment
abstract: Mining automation began in the 1960s to increase safety in underground mines. Today, robotic and autonomous systems perform specific mining activities, creating new oppor-tunities and a more efficient and safe industry. This paper proposes a novel solution for instrumentation for autonomous trucks working in open-pit mines, specifically during the parking maneuver to load ore. In this case, new hardware and firmware are developed to compute the future coordinates of the excavator bucket using two Global Positioning Systems (GPS) receivers. In this approach, employing the concept of geometry and information from the GPS receivers, the future coordinates of the excavator bucket are calculated and made available to control the system, parking the autonomous truck in the desired position. The results demonstrate the accurate positioning of the off-highway truck during the ore-loading process, allowing for the correct execution of the truck's autonomous positioning maneuver.

articleTitle: Heat Pump Management for Building's Indoor Temperature Control
abstract: In the present paper, an Advanced Process Control system for the optimized management of the heat pump power in a building is proposed. The considered process is characterized by four rooms and each room is equipped with a fan coil. A linear model of the process is derived through suitable identification procedures, considering the heat pump power and the outdoor temperature as Manipulated Variable and measured Input Disturbance Variable, respectively. The output of the model is represented by the temperature of each single room. A tailored formulation for the computation of an adaptive average temperature is proposed that takes into account users’ preferences and eventual detection of bad measurements. A Model Predictive Control strategy based on the formulated models represents the core of the Advanced Process Control system; the proposed controller aims to respect the imposed lower constraint on the rooms’ average temperature while ensuring heat pump power minimization when allowed. The proposed control system is tested on significant scenarios.

articleTitle: Development of Graphical User Application for Testing Lift Group Control Procedures Using Timer Object
abstract: The paper deals with the configuration of Timer Object in the App Designer environment of MATLAB product. User applications by default allow serial processing of program functions, which is not sufficient for the specific application design for logical control and animation of the movement of a group of lifts in a building. In order to be able to simultaneously perform animation and execute partial simple functions called when pressing buttons inside or outside the lift cabs, it was necessary to replace the parallel processing of functions with appropriate timing of the user application runtime. The non-standard approach to implementing program functions in user applications with timing settings may be useful for other similar visualization or monitoring problems.

articleTitle: Improving Industry 4.0 to Human-Centric Industry 5.0 in Light of the Protection of Human Rights
abstract: In this paper, we scrutinize the human-centricity pillar of Industry 5.0—a factor improving Industry 4.0—from the viewpoint of the protection of human rights, social and economic rights ensured by several international organizations and the European Union with the AI Act in the focal point. According to criticisms against Industry 4.0, the inherent social dimension, the well-being of workers, the need for social inclusion and the adoption of technologies that do not substitute, but rather complement human capabilities (whenever possible) are missing key elements. Therefore, the Industry 5.0 initiative adopted by the European Commission in 2021 is not to replace Industry 4.0 but complements it with three substantial requirements as follows: resilience, sustainability, and human-centricity. In this regard, the human-centricity of Industry 5.0 and the human-centric approach to the responsible and trustworthy AI overlap each other, since the human-centric approach has already been adopted for digital technologies, including artificial intelligence and is (or will be) a part of the EU legislation considering the AI Act—the world's first comprehensive AI law—and other related regulatory tools. The AI Act's human-centric approach is based on the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union and the values of the EU. An essential element of the document is the categorization of AI systems, which addresses the technology's inherent risk to society. On this basis, the AI Act distinguishes unacceptable (e.g., social scoring); high (e.g., recruitment, evaluating candidates, monitoring of workers) and minimal or no risk AI systems (e.g., spam filters). Therefore, the risk assessment of AI systems is cardinal to categorizing the technology before its operation. As society's inclusion is prominently observed through fundamental rights, another critical step is the impact assessment of fundamental rights in high-risk AI systems. This act is crucial to assess the relationship between technology and fundamental rights and examine its impact (whether it is acceptable or not) on human and social rights. Several international organizations and the EU have highlighted in their working documents the importance of protecting fundamental rights regarding AI (e.g., the right to equality and non-discrimination, which might be infringed by using the technology during employment decisions or recruitment). In conclusion, the analysis of the topic is pivotal as the use of AI systems is already part of our daily lives at home and the workplace.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Lower Limb Rehabilitation Robotic System
abstract: This paper presents the research carried out to design and develop a robotic system for the rehabilitation of the lower limbs. Therapists identified the need for a passive and active lower limb rehabilitation robotic system (LLRRS). The medical and technical requirements for an LLRRS were identified and analyzed. The concept of the project is to create an experimental model of an adaptive robotic system for the recovery of lower limbs (knee and ankle) with online access for the therapist/doctor. The design of the system was done in order for LLRRS to be used by patients in two situations: lying on a bed or sitting on a chair. At the same time, the design was done in order to adjust the LLRRS components’ dimensions according to the anthropometric dimensions of the lower limb to align the joints. The components were designed and achieved using a 3D printer or mechanical processing or chosen according to the design process. All the components were mechanically assembled and electrically connected, and the control algorithms were implemented in the chosen control unit and HMI. The design and development were user-centred processes.

articleTitle: Cascade PID Controllers Applied on Level and Flow Systems in a SMAR Didactic Plant

authors.preferredName: José Luís Sousa de Magalhães Lima

abstract: The practical application of knowledge acquired during undergraduate studies is crucial for students to address real-world problems and seek solutions. The SMAR PD3 didactic plant provides a conducive environment for experiments in systems such as level and flow, common in various industrial sectors. Cascade control, an approach that sequentially uses two or more controllers, stands out as a promising strategy to enhance precision and stability in industrial processes. This work proposes a study on cascade control in flow and level systems, demonstrating its application in the didactic plant. The process involved system identification, tuning of conventional and cascade PI and PID controllers, followed by the implementation of the Successive Loop Closure technique. Results, in line with specialized literature, indicate that the implementation of cascade controllers in the industry can improve specific processes affected by disturbances or changes in variables, directly impacting the overall functioning of the process.

articleTitle: WinterWatch: An Automated Approach to Outdoor Parking Lot Vacancy Detection in Cold Climates
abstract: The increasing demand for efficient parking space utilisation has triggered the development of vacancy detection systems, with a particular focus on addressing the unique environmental constraints imposed by winter conditions. In this paper we present vacancy detection tool trained on our dataset that was collected in the parking lot of the University of Zilina, capturing unique winter conditions from December to January. The dataset includes diverse weather scenarios, such as snowfall or early morning conditions where light is reflected directly into the camera. Leveraging YOLOv4, Faster R-CNN, and PKLot dataset, WinterWatch demonstrates good performance in real-time vacancy detection under these challenging circumstances. WinterWatch not only contributes to the evolution of smart parking systems but also underscores the importance of tailored solutions for diverse environmental settings, ensuring year-round efficiency in outdoor parking management.

articleTitle: Advanced Mathematical Modeling and Control Strategies for Autonomous Drone Systems
abstract: This paper explores the mathematical modelling and simulation of drones, focusing on both low-level and high-level control aspects. The low-level control involves altitude maintenance and stabilization, alongside disturbance compensation, essential for ensuring stable flight. At the high-level control, the research addresses compensating for air currents, drift correction, obstacle avoidance, localization, mapping, navigation to predefined points, returning to the take-off position (return to home), and person tracking. Additionally, it highlights the inherent limitations in drone usage, including restricted weight capacity, limited processing power, a constrained number of sensors, short battery life, rapid dynamics requiring electronic stabilization, continuous motion of the drone, and safety concerns. The study emphasizes the intricate interplay between mathematical models and control strategies to manage these control objectives and constraints. It delves into the development of mathematical models representing drone dynamics and sensor data fusion techniques. Simulation environments are utilized to validate and optimize control algorithms, replicating real-world scenarios to ensure reliable and robust drone performance. The paper aims to address these challenges by proposing mathematical modelling techniques and control strategies. By integrating sophisticated algorithms with limited hardware resources, it seeks to improve the efficiency and autonomy of drones while overcoming constraints. Ultimately, the research endeavours to contribute to the advancement of drone technology, enabling enhanced capabilities for various applications while ensuring safety and reliability.

articleTitle: Predictive Maintenance in Twin Screw Air Compressors through Unsupervised Learning
abstract: A predictive maintenance module for oil-injected twin screw compressors is proposed in the present paper. Oil-injected twin screw compressors are widely used in the pneumatic drive industry and their maintenance represents an important issue. In fact, periodic maintenance policies are exploited in this field; this practice can conduct to a decrease of the efficiency of the plant units where these devices are installed. In order to solve this problem, an unsupervised learning approach is proposed in order to design a predictive maintenance module. Reliable and significant data are acquired through an ad hoc data acquisition and storage system, based on Industry 4.0 principles. Data analysis represented a first crucial step for the exploitation of unsupervised learning methods. Three different operating conditions were taken into account, associated to the compressor's oil degradation. Satisfactory results in terms of accuracy were obtained in the tests of the developed module on real data.

articleTitle: Experimental Tests for an Innovative Catamaran Prototype: An Interesting Application Case
abstract: Autonomous Surface Vessels (ASVs) encounter diverse environmental conditions, from calm waters to turbulent scenarios with currents, winds, and waves. In challenging conditions, unmodeled dynamics threaten safety and reliability, surpassing conventional control capabilities. This study presents experimental results of constructing and controlling a catamaran-type ASV to address these challenges. The chosen catamaran design, known for stability and maneuverability, undergoes rigorous testing in varied conditions. The study delves into the complexities of ASV modeling, emphasizing dynamic behaviors crucial for effective control system design. Implemented model-based control strategies prove successful in mitigating unmodeled dynamics, and meeting stringent design requirements. Experimental results showcase the ASV's capability to navigate challenging environments safely and reliably.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Assist in Remote Operation of Nursing Mobile Robot
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study on the integration and effects of machine learning assist in the remote operation of a nursing mobile robot, a crucial tool in the evolving landscape of healthcare technology. We begin by outlining the growing need for advanced robotic assistance in nursing, driven by challenges such as an aging population and a global shortfall in healthcare staff. The study is divided into two main sections: simulation-based research and experimental trials. In the simulation-based research, we develop and test a machine learning assist algorithm within a virtual environment, aimed at improving the precision and safety of remote nursing robot operations. This section includes an analysis of the robot's performance in tasks requiring delicate manipulation, like ad-ministering medication. The experimental trials are conducted using a prototype nursing robot equipped with machine learning assisted controller. These trials involve real-world scenarios, such as navigating through hospital corridors and performing basic nursing tasks. The effectiveness of machine learning assist algorithm could be evaluated in terms of operator accuracy in obstacle avoidance. Our results demonstrate that incorporating machine learning assist significantly enhances the efficiency and safety of remote nursing robot operations. Operators reported improved control and greater confidence in performing delicate tasks, leading to a higher standard of patient care.

articleTitle: Enhancing Photovoltaic Array Performance under Partial Shading through Dynamic Reconfiguration and Layer Equalization Algorithm
abstract: Partial shading (PS) significantly impacts the performance of photovoltaic (PV) systems, leading to reduced efficiency. Traditional mitigation methods involve bypass diodes or PV module reconfiguration. Accordingly, the highest and lowest layer-based exchange (HLLBE) algorithm was proposed. The HLLBE system employs a Switching Block Array (SBA) for flexible reconfiguration without rewiring. By sorting and swapping irradiance readings, the HLLBE algorithm achieves uniform current distribution across PV array layers. Unlike static configurations, HLLBE dynamically adapts to shade patterns, offering an efficient solution. Simulations on a 3 × 3 PV array demonstrated HLLBE's effectiveness in enhancing output power and reducing multiple peaks compared to conventional total-cross-tied (TCT) configurations. Additionally, HLLBE minimizes operating switches through a switching matrix during dynamic reconfiguration (DR).

articleTitle: The Comparison of Machine Vision Approaches for Standard Industrial Solutions
abstract: Stereovision (2D), the most frequently used approach for implementing inspection tasks, proves its usability through many practical solutions in SME enterprises. There are several reasons, starting with economic ones and ending with implementation into an actual process. Due to this, our article aims to compare suitable camera system for recognizing the selected sensed object properties. Also, there is a realisation of the inspection tasks such as reading text, bar-codes, or finding (counting) an object in the field of vision scene with the 60% minimum matching and execution duration up to 25 [ms]. Besides, the authors want to point out a systematically oriented solution suitable for commercial enterprises based 90% recognition success, and max twelve products finding. By using and combining software modules into the 2D camera system, was proven the theoretical findings and then realized their experimental testing directly at an actual workplace. Moreover, by comparing the obtained values, it is possible to recommend a combination of industrial inspection applications to the required task and the success score. Also, part of the article compares individual types of inspection detection, considering their complexity or knowledge of programming language.

articleTitle: Describing and Applying the Entity Framework from Simple Applications to Complex Scenarios. Case Study
abstract: Object-relational mapping (ORM) is considered today a method used in computer systems for data conversion based on object-oriented programming languages. This technique involves a “database of virtual objects” that can be used with the support of the programming language. Currently, both free (open source) and commercial packages that perform ORM can be used. In practice, it is common for some programmers to build their ORM tools. In languages that permit object-oriented programming, the entire architecture of the programs is designated as an architecture of objects and the relationships between them. The management of data, or information, refers to the methods of access and management of objects that are almost always non-scalar values. This article will present the utility of the Entity Framework for common implementation scenarios starting from systems for car sales sites or standard applications and up to the development of complex systems for managing information flows for critical systems. Moreover, the transition from the object-oriented development model to practical applications will be presented. The main advantages and disadvantages of the development environment and technology based on Asp. net will be also discussed. In conclusion, the article represents a transition from the description of the Entity Framework to the integration and application of this system in some practical applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Livestock Food Monitoring System
abstract: In the context of optimizing herd management and animal health monitoring, this study aims to enhance the understanding of livestock feeding behavior through precise monitoring of the time each animal spends at the trough. The primary objective is to optimize feed supply management while concurrently enabling early detection of potential health issues. The fundamental innovation of this study revolves around the creation of an Internet of Things (IoT) Platform, leveraging Ultra High Frequency (UHF) Radio-Frequency Identification (RFID) tags and a specialized antenna cable. This platform facilitates the meticulous recording of animals' ingress and egress times at the feeding trough, thereby providing valuable insights for improved livestock management and health monitoring.

articleTitle: Experiments on Detecting and Monitoring Objects based on Thermal Imaging
abstract: Object detection and tracking on RGB and thermal imaging is getting increasingly more advanced and important in the field of computer vision. The increasing image quality combined with decreasing camera prices during recent years, created new opportunities to gather data. They are now used in many different fields, for example: medical, military, law enforcement or industrial applications. Thermal cameras are useful in darkness and in situations when there is not enough light for cameras that operate in the visual spectrum to function properly. Leveraging the information provided by colored images for labeling, this paper approach aims to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of object recognition in thermal imagery. The synergy between thermal and colored imagery offers a comprehensive solution, addressing challenges posed by limited thermal resolution and ambiguity in object boundaries. By harnessing the complementary strengths of colored and thermal imaging, this paper opens avenues for applications in surveillance, autonomous systems, and other fields where reliable object detection and tracking under challenging thermal conditions are paramount. For this experiment different models were trained using MMDetection and MMRotate modules from MMLab framework. We explored and compared multiple models like: Rotated Faster R-CNN (two-stage anchor-based detection), Single Shot Alignment Network (S2ANET one stage anchor detector), and FCOSR (one-stage anchor-free detector)

articleTitle: Integrating Servopress Acoustic Monitoring with Machine Learning for Enhanced Predictive Maintenance: Opportunities and Limitations
abstract: This paper explores the innovative integration of acoustic monitoring of servo presses with machine learning algorithms to improve predictive maintenance strategies in industrial environments. Our research focuses on the application of advanced acoustic sensors to capture and analyze servo press acoustic data, which is critical in forming and pressing operations. This acoustic data serves as a key indicator of machine health, potentially revealing signs of wear or failure before they occur. We present the implementation of machine learning models trained on historical acoustic data, highlighting how these models can identify patterns indicative of machine degradation. The goal of this predictive approach is to optimize maintenance schedules, reduce downtime and extend the lifetime of industrial equipment. It also addresses the inherent challenges and limitations of applying artificial intelligence in this field. These include issues related to the quality and quantity of data required for accurate modelling, the complexity of real industrial environments, the ongoing need for AI system maintenance, and the risks associated with over-reliance on automated systems. Our findings suggest that while integrating servo press acoustic monitoring with machine learning offers significant potential for improving predictive maintenance, it requires a balanced approach that combines technological innovation with human expertise. The paper concludes with recommendations for future research and practical implementation strategies in industrial settings.

articleTitle: Association of Relevant Anatomic Contours of Ultrasound and MRI Images by Optimisation via Different Geometric Parameters
abstract: We focus on the simultaneous analysis and harmonisation of 2D dynamic ultrasound and MRI records, the aim of which is to find a biunique correspondence between the radial geometry of the ultrasound frames and the rectangular geometry of the MRI frames. One possible way of adjusting the two sources is the bidirectional conversion of the relevant anatomic contours of the oral cavity. We implemented this idea by the construction of special geometric transformations acting on the tongue and palate contours fitted automatically to the boundaries of the different tissues visualised by the ultrasound and MRI images. The transformations include the magnification and rotation of the curves, determining a given set of parameters. We create such optimisation techniques with which the average distance between the corresponding ultrasound and MRI contours can be minimised fixed by the most favourable values of the parameter set defined by the geometric transformations. By executing these operations, the ultrasound contours can be projected onto the MRI frames, and vice versa. We validate our results by visual and numerical considerations, as well.

articleTitle: Design and Control of a Magnetic-Wheeled Climbing Robot for Vertical Steel Surfaces: Motor Positioning Performance Through Model Reference Adaptive Control
abstract: Climbing robots capable of performing activities on vertical steel walls are frequently utilized in the maintenance of high-rise structures and unsafe situations for human workers, including bridges, ships, liquid tanks, chimneys, pipelines, nuclear facilities, and wind turbines. A climbing robot outfitted with the necessary equipment performs activities such as monitoring, cleaning, search and rescue, and more. The fundamental aim is to design a sturdy and safe robotic system with an adhesion-to-the-wall approach that can move on the surface while carrying the essential sensing system, actuation, and drive system as power cables or suppliers. The principal restrictions are the large forces that appear in the system and directly affect the motors. This paper presents a climbing robot design with magnetic wheels powered by a direct current motor; a simplified model with experimental parameter identification is utilized, and a model incorporating all forces is used to develop and test a model reference adaptive controller. Coulomb friction, magnetic forces that hold the system to the wall, and the gravity force are defined as the parts of the overall disturbance. A well-designed motion controller must be accurate enough to drive the robot's trajectory while also being robust enough to withstand overall disturbances. It must also take into account the limited control signal and saturation related with the servomotors. MATLAB/Simulink is used to identify experimental parameters and simulate various control scenarios.

articleTitle: Project and Design of a Catamaran Prototype with Aerial Propulsion System
abstract: This paper outlines the innovative design and project details of an Autonomous Surface Vehicle with catamaran topology, specifically engineered for lake inspections. The primary focus is on integrating aerial propulsion systems to enhance operational efficiency and mobility in lacustrine environments. The design incorporates advanced electronic architecture, integrating autonomous navigation systems and specialized sensors for comprehensive data collection. This technological synergy enables the catamaran to conduct precise inspections, monitoring environmental factors, water quality, and other relevant variables. In summary, the proposed autonomous catamaran offers an innovative solution for lake inspections, combining advanced mobility and precise data collection. This project has the potential not only to optimize environmental monitoring operations but also to significantly contribute to the preservation and sustainable management of lacustrine ecosystems.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control of the Van De Vusse Reaction: Comparing the Deterministic and Stochastic State Estimation
abstract: This paper deals with the design of model predictive control (MPC) for a nonlinear model of a Van de Vusse reaction, that has been linearized at specific operating points. Since the conventional MPC formulation requires the full state vector, it is necessary to design a state observer that estimates the unmeasurable states of the system. Due to the fact that the accuracy of the state estimation significantly affects the resulting performance of MPC, the aim of this study is to compare the designed control while considering two different approaches to the state estimation. In particular, the Luenberger state observer and the Kalman filter are studied in this paper. The Luenberger observer represents the deterministic state estimator, that considers a system without significant noise affecting the states and the output, while its design is based on the pole placement method. In contrast, the statistically optimal state estimator is based on the Kalman filter design to estimate the state in the case of stochastic systems. The rest of the paper presents the results of simulations of MPC applied to the Van de Vusse reaction model using both considered state estimators.

articleTitle: From Data to Decisions: AdaBoost-based Approach for Remaining useful Life Estimation
abstract: In today's industrial environment, the proactive management of assets has a crucial role in ensuring operational efficiency and mitigating unforeseen downtime. This proactive approach is based on the ability to accurately estimate the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of critical components and systems. This paper overviews the known approaches to support decision making in maintenance. The study involves the analysis of operational data, utilizing predictive models to forecast the remaining lifespan of critical assets. An AdaBoost-based prediction approach is presented. The integration of machine data-driven RUL predictions promises to revolutionize asset management practices, providing industries with a powerful tool to mitigate downtime and improve resource allocation.

articleTitle: Vector Fields Autonomous Control for Assistive Mobile Robots
abstract: This study introduces an innovative autonomous control system for assistive mobile robots, focusing on users with significant physical disabilities. Leveraging vector fields and a modified A* algorithm, the system enhances the traditional approach to robotic wheelchair navigation. The methodology emphasizes autonomous navigation in familiar environments, integrating advanced Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs) for user interaction and control. Experimental analysis demonstrates the system's superiority over conventional Proportional, Integral and Derivative (PID) controllers in terms of safety, adaptability, and user comfort. The solution effectively addresses the challenges of map maintenance, route planning, and dynamic obstacle avoidance, marking a significant advancement in assistive robotics.

articleTitle: Reinforcement Learning Approach to Adaptive Traffic Signal Control Using SUMO-RL
abstract: Traffic control in urban environments is a complex and critical challenge, with growing urbanisation and increasing vehicular congestion necessitating innovative solutions. Reinforcement learning has emerged as a promising approach to optimise traffic control and improve overall transportation efficiency, thanks to its ability to grasp the intricacies of complex issues without human involvement autonomously. In this paper, we propose a modified version of the SUMO-RL package and demonstrate its advantages in the context of our ongoing research regarding traffic control in the city of Zilina. The proposed modifications include support for custom reward functions for different agents and custom observation functions, representing a crucial design component when solving traffic signal control as a multi-agent reinforcement learning problem. We also present our preliminary results, which demonstrate the potential of reinforcement learning in addressing traffic control challenges.

articleTitle: Agriculture Rotary Tedder Fault Diagnosis using Multiple Input - Multiple Type - Parallel - Convolutional Neural Network Optimized by Genetic Algorithm
abstract: For several years, fault diagnosis methods have been increasingly using methods based on neural networks. These methods have many advantages, but the process of creating their architecture, training and testing requires a lot of expert knowledge and is time-consuming, especially when building a neural network by trial and error, as is usually done with new types of machines. For this reason, we propose an innovative method to solve this problem by automating the previously mentioned steps of building a neural network, adapting it to the available data and selecting the best training method. Automation is carried out using an appropriately adapted genetic algorithm that generates the entire architecture of the neural network, and this neural network can have multiple inputs, have parallel input data processing paths and handle different types of input data at the same time. Our algorithm was tested using highly noisy data from a field agricultural rotary tedder, and the resulting neural networks were able to detect the type of machine fault with an accuracy of over 80%.

articleTitle: Automation in Clinical Laboratories: A Comprehensive Bibliography Review
abstract: Laboratory automation has become essential for the survival of laboratories in today's market. The pursuit of efficiency among companies operating in the laboratory sector extends to encompass all analytical phases of processes. This study aims to provide a review of automation processes in clinical analysis laboratories. It is a literature review that included a search in the Lilacs, Scielo, and Scopus databases. Technological advances have enabled laboratories of various sizes and examination volumes to incorporate some level of automation into their processes. This is because manually performed steps require more execution time and are prone to errors. Automation emerges as a solution capable of enhancing the accuracy of analyses, resulting in greater operational efficiency for the laboratory. The key lies in choosing the best model based on the laboratory's reality, aiming to reduce costs and increase the quality and objectivity of services, thereby adding more value to the customer.

articleTitle: Application of Teleoperation Control for a Robotic Hand using a Glove
abstract: The use of the robotic hand has spread widely in recent times, as it has set foot in a wide variety of fields, such as the medical, military, and industrial, and has become greater complexity, developed, faster, and more efficient, thanks to the communication technology, where the world of communications has been marked by two revolutions: the Internet and mobile telephony, where the internet connectivity was integrated into the cellular network in the early 2000s through data services such as GPRS. These systems provide end-user benefits in terms of reach and mobility. Currently, tele-operation via the Internet takes its status in the remote control of complex mechanical systems with several degrees of freedom, thanks to increasingly powerful communication protocols, numerous studies and research have been carried out around robotics, some of them are complex, expensive, inefficient, and some are restricted or limited. On this ground, we implemented a suitable, uncomplicated, inexpensive design with good efficiency and high response. In this paper, an industrial robotic hand was developed and designed that printed by a 3D printer, which is controlled wirelessly by wearable glove-embedded flex sensors. The robotic hand simulates human hand finger movements (hand gestures) with the ability to hold things well very similar to the real hand. The design consists of two main parts, the first part (server or receiver part) the robotic hand and its components (electronic circuit design), consisting of five servo motors linked to a microcontroller Arduino Uno for the purpose of moving robotic fingers, where a single servo motor is assigned to each finger, with the XBee signal receiving unit, which is installed on the Arduino by a special shield, the second part (the master or sender part) the glove built-in with flexible sensors that worn by the person, this circuit consists of sensors (flexible printed resistance) connected with ordinary variable resistors in the form of a voltage divider circuit and attached with the Arduino LilyPad where it sends signals to the robotic hand using the XBee transmitter module(radio frequency).

articleTitle: eCall Systems: Enhancing Safety and Accessibility
abstract: The eCall system is the EU's ultimate response to provide rapid assistance automatically or at the push of a button in the event of an accident or emergency situation. With access to numerous onboard sensors, the eCall system has become a pivotal component since 2018. In this paper, we first examine the latest advancements in eCall-compatible devices and systems suitable for cars manufactured before 2018 in the EU. We also present data on seat belt usage as part of our passenger counting analysis. Additionally, we discuss and analyse the eCall system's applicability to vehicle types other than personal vehicles. Finally, we propose a cost-effective concept for a retrofit passenger detection system for older vehicles utilising simple seat belt buckle connector and film pressure sensors.

articleTitle: Wastewater Pumping Stations Retrofitting. Development of a Brownfield Industry 4.0 Solution
abstract: In the water industry, digitalization and Industry 4.0 have become a favorite subject. New projects and solutions based on Industry 4.0 principles have been developed and can be found integrated in numerous water control systems. But a main topic is the applicability at the level of the control systems built in the past, which are still operating today. Many of these were built without digitalization, autonomous process optimization, or remote communication. The actual wastewater networks must manage many difficult situations due to increases in population, sometimes using the same infrastructure or inflow of stormwater. Therefore, they must prevent overflows, flooding streets, discharging untreated sewage into local waterways. Breakdowns at a sewerage pump station may involve environmental incidents and the costs of a breakdown repair are far higher than maintenance tasks. Energy, maintenance and operation costs are responsible for half of the total LCC (Life cycle cost) of a wastewater pumping station. This material proposes a specific approach for the control systems of existing wastewater pumping stations in municipal areas, to integrate the principles of Industry 4.0 digitalization, with the main goal of reducing LCC, as well as the number of unforeseen events. Another plus is that the proposed retrofitting concepts are transferable to other application purposes.

articleTitle: Air Quality Monitoring and Photovoltaic Impact Assessment in Valea Jiului
abstract: This paper focuses on air pollution in Jiul Valley, a region characterized by mining activities and extensive use of coal for household heating, especially during the cold season. To assess this issue, the use of an MQ-7 sensor network is proposed. These sensors, integrated into an extended network, have been employed to collect data on carbon monoxide (CO) concentrations in the air. Additionally, the utilization of a Raspberry Pi device is proposed, allowing the collected data to be processed and used to generate interactive maps. Initial data analysis has highlighted significant variations in CO concentrations depending on location and seasonal changes, with higher levels in proximity to residential and industrial areas. Furthermore, the study proposes an expansion of monitoring to investigate the impact of airborne pollutants on the performance of photovoltaic panels. Future plans include implementing a photovoltaic panel system on the former waste heaps in Jiul Valley. This expansion of the research aims to explore the relationship between atmospheric pollution levels and the energy efficiency of photovoltaic panels, especially within the context of the mining region. These preliminary findings emphasize not only the importance of implementing effective monitoring and intervention strategies to reduce pollution but also the relevance of investigating pollution's impact on future sustainable technologies such as photovoltaic panels. Moreover, this work provides an initial perspective on the capabilities of MQ-7 sensors in air pollution monitoring and serves as a foundation for further development of efficient air quality management strategies in Jiul Valley and similar regions, considering the prospective integration of sustainable technologies.

articleTitle: Comparison of Bio-Inspired Algorithms in a Case Study for Optimizing Capacitor Bank Allocation in Electrical Power Distribution
abstract: This paper investigates the Fish School Search (FSS) algorithm's effectiveness for optimizing capacitor placement in electrical distribution networks, focusing on the challenges of increasing demand and aging infrastructures. The study assesses FSS's unique capability to evade local optima, contrasting its performance with established methods like Ant Colony (AC), Constructive Heuristic Algorithm (CHA), and Genetic Algorithm (GA) in various systems, including IEEE-14, IEEE-33, and IEEE-69 buses. Results highlight FSS's superior performance in reducing active losses, using fewer resources and iterations. This research underscores the potential of bio-inspired algorithms in complex power distribution challenges and suggests new directions for algorithmic efficiency and broader application.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Innovative Workplaces for Education in the Field of Smart Technologies with a Focus on Control and Computer Systems
abstract: The paper deals with innovative approaches in engineering education, especially in the field of control and computer systems with an emphasis on the integration of Smart technologies. As part of the research project implemented in the Laboratory of Production Processes Digitization, three specialized workplaces were developed. They provide students with a unique platform for experimentation and innovation in control and computer systems. The first workplace is focused on practical teaching of the Smart technologies basics, where students can construct and program their own Smart systems. We emphasize the importance of a hands-on approach in engineering education, which allows students not only to acquire theoretical knowledge, but also to develop practical skills in the field of design and systems engineering implementation. The second workplace focuses on applications of Smart technologies in homes. Here, students analyze and investigate the interactions among different components of Smart systems, thereby gaining important knowledge about the integration and coordination of control systems in real conditions. The third workplace focuses on Smart industrial applications and contains complex technological equipment, including industrial computers, Internet of Things (IoT) modules and peripherals for programmable logic control units (PLC). This workplace offers students the opportunity to design and implement sophisticated control systems for automated processes, expanding their skills in industrial automation and control technologies. Overall, this paper provides a thorough insight into innovative methods in engineering education and highlights how the integration of Smart technologies into educational programs contributes to the development of student competencies. These competencies are critically important to prepare future engineers for the challenges and needs of the modern industrial and business environment.

articleTitle: Utilizing Image Recognition Methods for the Identification and Counting of Live Nematodes in Petri Dishes
abstract: This article addresses a system designed for identifying and quantifying several species of nematodes, free-living and parasitic, placed on Petri dishes using modern image recognition methods. Traditional methods of counting nematodes are often time-consuming and prone to errors, leading to inaccurate biological and ecological study results. Our method employs advanced machine learning algorithms and computer vision to detect and count live nematodes automatically. The process utilizes algorithms to recognize specific larval characteristics, such as size and shape. This allows for high accuracy and efficiency while minimizing human intervention. The results demonstrate that our approach is robust and precise and can be widely utilized in biological research and applications.

articleTitle: Ultrasound- and MRI-based Speech Synthesis Applying Neural Networks
abstract: Starting from 2D dynamic ultrasound and MRI sources recording the movement of the vocal organs and the speech signal of the speaker in a simultaneous and synchronised manner, we produce machine speech by means of artificial intelligence. As visual objects, we use tongue and palate contours fitted automatically to the anatomic boundaries of the ultrasound and MRI images, and for training, we extract geometric information from these contours, as the change of their shape fundamentally describes the movement of the vocal organs during articulation. The geometric data consist of radial distances between the tongue and palate contours and coefficients of the discrete cosine transform of the curves, respectively. Relying on this dataset, parameters connected to the acoustic content of the speech signal are trained by the network. These parameters can be interpreted in the framework of the acoustic tube model of the vocal tract, and according to this, reflection coefficients and areas of the articulation channel are to be trained. In this study, vowels, words, and sentences are synthesised using linear predictive coding and the acoustic tube model.
